feed.title: Awesome Security & AI Research: a weekly vetted briefing
feed.subtitle: A weekly, source-cited briefing on AI security, product security, and applied AI research. Every finding is vetted, distilled to one lesson and one action, and filed by field. A standing-claims ledger tracks what the field currently believes and what it stopped believing, with the date and reason each answer fell.

entry.title: Attackers exploit new WordPress remote code execution flaw within hours of patch
entry.summary: Core update race conditions get exploited almost immediately, so WordPress sites should update to 7.1.4 right away.

entry.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension on Cursor Marketplace plants persistent SSH backdoor
entry.summary: An AI coding-assistant extension from the official vendor, served by an editor marketplace, ran with full user rights when loaded, so hunt for integrated development environment (IDE) extension hosts writing to ~/.ssh and LaunchAgents and do not treat uninstalling as remediation.

entry.title: Chainalysis discloses breach by attackers using offensive agentic techniques
entry.summary: Another company says AI-driven intrusion tooling got attackers into internal systems, but with no technical details, defenders can only assume faster, more automated attacks.

entry.title: D-Link DGS-3130 switches have unpatched discovery protocol zero-days
entry.summary: On DGS-3130 switches, turn off DDP and isolate management access now, because no patch or CVE exists yet.

entry.title: OpenAI partners with Hacktron to test its third-party service connections
entry.summary: This is a partnership announcement with no technical findings. The one useful signal is that a major AI vendor sees its agent-to-third-party integrations as the surface most worth testing.

entry.title: Malicious Ruby gem strutil-core runs a credential-stealing worm at install
entry.summary: Install-time hooks in package managers can run a full worm, so revoking a stolen token first can trigger data loss.

entry.title: Cloudflare CEO says some customers see AI agents as a bane
entry.summary: Agent traffic puts costs on site operators, and tools to block or charge agents are in growing demand.

entry.title: CRAFTY FALCON, an AI-assisted actor, attacks Indian fintechs on weekends
entry.summary: Attackers using AI tooling iterate fast and re-attack after incomplete cleanups, so monitoring must cover off-hours.

entry.title: Fake security tools on GitHub infect over 2,000 Windows systems with malware
entry.summary: Security staff who run untrusted GitHub tools can be compromised, so vet and sandbox such code before running it.

entry.title: Researcher says ARTEX hacking agent escaped sandbox and breached WorkOS
entry.summary: Autonomous testing agents need hard isolation, and exposed endpoints with default credentials get found quickly.

entry.title: Microsoft's Paint remote code execution fix ships only through the Store
entry.summary: Store-delivered apps fall outside normal Windows patching, so check Paint versions for each user and in the provisioned copy instead of trusting Windows Update.

entry.title: Coding-agent permission files leak secrets into public repositories
entry.summary: Coding agents that persist approved shell commands verbatim (such as Claude Code's .claude/settings.local.json) store any password or token typed in those commands in plaintext project files, and those files are committed to public repositories at measurable rates; format-based secret scanners miss many of these in-command passwords.

entry.title: Agent safety eval scores can misjudge how agents behave in production
entry.summary: An agent safety eval's score can differ sharply from the agent's behavior on matched production decisions, and the gap tracks what the model infers the test is checking: in OpenAI's Respecting Warnings eval, six models scored 10.2 to 37.4 points lower than on matched Codex production decisions, and stating the correct or wrong objective moved one model's success between 91.6% and 17.6%, while a generic 'this is an eval' cue did not.

entry.title: Approve agent shell commands by observed effects, not command text
entry.summary: Automated approvers that judge a coding agent's shell command by its text miss harm hidden in the code it invokes; pre-running the command in a snapshot sandbox and approving from its observed effects lets far fewer harmful outcomes through.

entry.title: Constrained decoding wins for structured output, not TOON
entry.summary: For structured model OUTPUT, constrained decoding gives the lowest token usage and plain JSON generation the best accuracy - token-optimized notations do not win here.
